<div class="ci" id="cahspar-explorer">

  <h1>Working life.<br>Shared wellbeing.</h1>
  <p class="ci-lead">A multidimensional view of working life and social policy, with Türkiye at its centre.</p>
  <p>Explore six connected dimensions of a fairer, more sustainable world of work.</p>
  <a class="ci-primary" href="#explore">Explore the prototype <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
  <a class="ci-text-link" href="#methodology">Read the proposed approach →</a></div>
  <div class="ci-framework" aria-label="The six dimensions of the proposed index"><span class="ci-eyebrow">ONE FRAMEWORK · SIX DIMENSIONS</span><div class="ci-framework-row"><span>01</span><strong>Working life</strong></div><div class="ci-framework-row"><span>02</span><strong>Social policy</strong></div><div class="ci-framework-row"><span>03</span><strong>Equality and inclusion</strong></div><div class="ci-framework-row"><span>04</span><strong>Welfare</strong></div><div class="ci-framework-row"><span>05</span><strong>Sustainability</strong></div><div class="ci-framework-row"><span>06</span><strong>The future of work</strong></div></div>
</header>
<div class="ci-notice" role="note"><strong>Demonstration · synthetic data</strong><span>Every score, rank and trend below is invented to demonstrate the interface. No official ÇAHSPAR results have been published. Years refer to sample data, not publication editions.</span></div>
<nav class="ci-section-nav" aria-label="Index sections"><a href="#explore">01 / Explore</a><a href="#dimensions">02 / Dimensions</a><a href="#methodology">03 / Methodology</a><a href="#sources">04 / Data sources</a></nav>
<section id="explore" aria-labelledby="explore-title">

A connected picture.</h2><p>A sample international comparison to test the experience. The final coverage is still to be agreed.</p></div><button id="ci-download" class="ci-button" disabled>Download demo CSV ↓</button></div>
  <div id="ci-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">Loading the demonstration…</div>

    <div class="ci-toolbar">
      <label>Find a country<input id="ci-search" type="search" placeholder="Search by country name" autocomplete="off"></label>

<section id="dimensions"><p class="ci-eyebrow">THE PROPOSED FRAMEWORK</p><h2>Six lenses on working life and social policy</h2><p>These dimensions follow the association’s original Index brief. Indicators below are candidates for consultation, not an approved measurement framework.</p><div class="ci-dimension-grid"><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">01</span><h3>Working life</h3><p>Employment, job quality, wages and working conditions.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Employment-to-population ratio</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">02</span><h3>Social policy</h3><p>Social protection, social security and access to services.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Social protection coverage</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">03</span><h3>Equality and inclusion</h3><p>Participation and opportunity across population groups.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Gender employment gap</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">04</span><h3>Welfare</h3><p>Income, poverty and living conditions.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>At-risk-of-poverty rate</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">05</span><h3>Sustainability</h3><p>Sustainable working lives and social resilience.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Excessive working hours</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">06</span><h3>The future of work</h3><p>Digital skills, technological change and new forms of work.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Basic or above-basic digital skills</strong></p></article></div></section>
<section id="methodology" class="ci-method"><div><p class="ci-eyebrow">TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN</p><h2>From indicators to insight</h2><p>The Index aims to make developments measurable, comparable and trackable for researchers, decision-makers, public bodies and civil society.</p><a href="assets/index/indicator-candidates.csv" download>Download candidate indicator dictionary (CSV) ↓</a></div><div><ol><li><strong>Define the indicators.</strong> Confirm relevance, coverage and comparability with subject specialists.</li><li><strong>Document each observation.</strong> Record its source, unit, reference period, population and revision status.</li><li><strong>Agree the calculation.</strong> Publish direction, normalisation, weights, missing-data rules and sensitivity checks before releasing results.</li><li><strong>Publish reproducible results.</strong> Release versioned data, calculation rules and a methodology report together.</li></ol><p class="ci-method-note"><strong>Not yet decided:</strong> geographic coverage, baseline, indicator set, weighting and aggregation. The prototype’s 0–100 scores and equal weights are interface assumptions only. Missing values must never silently become zero.</p></div></section>
<section id="sources"><p class="ci-eyebrow">EVIDENCE BEFORE RANKINGS</p><h2>Planned institutional data sources</h2><p>The original brief identifies the institutions below. Their inclusion here does not imply a data agreement, verified indicator coverage or endorsement. <footer class="ci-footer"><p><strong>A research programme in progress.</strong> The next milestone is an agreed methodology and a documented pilot dataset for Türkiye.</p><a href="iletisim.html">Contribute to the Index →</a></footer>
